findings.issue: No auditService.log call after TaskComment create. Every write in the established pattern (employees.service.ts) is audited; addComment is a write that is silently unaudited.
findings.consequence: Comment writes bypass the audit log, breaking the audit trail for task activity.
findings.correction: After taskComment.create, call await this.auditService.log({ tenantId, actorId: authorId, action: 'task.comment.added', resourceType: 'TaskComment', resourceId: comment.id, outcome: 'SUCCESS' }).

findings.location: addMember, removeMember, addMilestone, updateMilestone, addStatusUpdate methods
findings.issue: None of these five write operations call auditService.log. Additionally addMember and removeMember have no actorId parameter, so the actor cannot be recorded even if a call were added.
findings.consequence: Project member, milestone, and status-update mutations are entirely unaudited. Security-relevant membership changes (addMember/removeMember) cannot be attributed to an actor.
findings.correction: Thread actorId: string into addMember, removeMember, addMilestone, updateMilestone; update research.controller.ts to pass user.sub; add auditService.log after each write.

findings.location: review() method, after findFirst, before update
findings.issue: No status guard checks that result.status === SUBMITTED before applying the review transition. A DRAFT or already-APPROVED result can be reviewed or returned.
findings.consequence: A user with performance.results.review permission can return or review a result that was never submitted, corrupting the KPI workflow state.
findings.correction: Add: if (result.status !== KpiResultStatus.SUBMITTED) { throw new BadRequestException(`Cannot review a result with status ${result.status}`); }

findings.location: approve() method, after findFirst, before update
findings.issue: No status guard checks result.status before applying APPROVED. A DRAFT, RETURNED, or already-APPROVED result can be directly approved.
findings.consequence: A user with performance.results.approve permission can approve a DRAFT result, bypassing submission and review steps entirely.
findings.correction: Add a guard asserting the expected prior status (SUBMITTED, or REVIEWED if a two-step review workflow is intended) and throw BadRequestException on violation.

findings.issue: The ProjectStatusUpdate record is created without a tenantId field. If ProjectStatusUpdate has its own tenantId column in the schema, rows will be missing tenant context, breaking direct table queries for tenant scoping.
findings.consequence: Status update records lack tenant isolation; any query on ProjectStatusUpdate filtered by tenantId will omit these rows.
findings.correction: Add tenantId to the data object: { researchProjectId: projectId, content, authorId, tenantId }. Verify the field exists in the Prisma schema first; if absent, file a schema migration and close this finding.
